biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Taxonomic biomarkers were identified to each South American traditional group studied, including each Yanomami group.
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers include specific bacterial genera like Escherichia, Ralstonia (Yanomami/Brazil), Neisseria, Desulfovibrio (Yanomami/Venezuela), Cutibacterium, Akkermansia, and archaeal genera.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: LDA score of >4.0 were used as thresholds. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) was performed using LEfSe
biomarker_unit.notes: Biomarkers identified via LDA with LDA score >4.0; abundance measured as percentage relative abundance.

value: Yanomami/Brazil: Escherichia (high abundance), Ralstonia (high abundance), Cutibacterium, Akkermansia, Treponema, Brachyspira
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Escherichia and Ralstonia genera in the Yanomami/Brazil, and therefore, they were defined as Yanomami/Brazil biomarkers. On the other hand, Neisseria and Desulfovibrio were defined as Yanomami/Venezuela biomarkers, while Klebsiella was the biomarker of the Matses group.
biomarker_value.notes: Biomarker taxa identified through LDA analysis; Yanomami/Brazil also shows higher abundance of virulence, motility/chemotaxis, and regulation/cell signaling functions.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Stool samples collected but phenotype measurements (consistency, form, etc.) not reported; focus is on microbiome composition and function.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: No tumor measurements; no cancer patients in this microbiome study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: This study focused on gut microbiome characterization in hunter-gatherer populations, not tumor studies. Field is not applicable.

value: Comparative study across multiple populations (Brazil Yanomami, Venezuela Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco, US urban)
